title: School and College Enrollment Validation
text:
This site validates the PopulationSim synthetic population — the household/person microdata underlying WFRC’s travel demand model — against real K-12 and college enrollment, for the Wasatch Front region (Box Elder, Davis, Weber, Salt Lake, and Utah counties). School enrollment is compared at the school district level; college enrollment at the county level.
PopulationSim doesn’t control on school enrollment directly, so each comparison is made two ways: against the synthetic population’s uncontrolled enrollment-status label (the real test of how well the synthetic population reflects actual enrollment), and against its controlled age-band population (a sanity bound — age-eligible should meet or exceed enrolled, not match it exactly).

title: Synthetic Population
text:
This script produces the “synthetic” half of the validation schema: PopulationSim’s estimate of how many K-12 students and college students live in each district and county, to compare against the real enrollment numbers from 2_enrollment.qmd.

Objective: count synthetic persons by school district and by county, to compare with DOE and NCES. By district: sch_grade (every person with SCHG 1-14, at any age, matching DOE’s totalk12 + preschool and NCES’s K-12 + PK) and age_3_18 (every person aged 3-18, counted independently, a sanity bound since age is controlled in PopulationSim). By county: sch_grade (SCHG 15 or higher, any age) and age_18_24 (population aged 18-24, a sanity bound).
What it reads: PopulationSim’s synthetic person output (local-only, under _data/raw/populationsim/ABM/1_Inputs/ScenarioBaseSample/1_PopulationSim/output/, gitignored). The dorm and group-quarters students are in the same file, so no second file is needed. It also reads the school and college crosswalks from 1_geography.qmd.
MAZ join: each person has a maz_id. The MAZ rows in crosswalk_school.csv give each person a school district, and the MAZ rows in crosswalk_college.csv give each person a county.
Known gaps: college counts are residence-based and include every enrolled resident, while IPEDS counts by institution location and USHE counts public institutions only. The two sides differ in definition, not only in data.
Box Elder: handled last. The MPO/TDM model region only partly covers the county, so its synthetic counts need to be clipped to the model boundary (1_geography.qmd’s model_boundary layer) before comparison. This is still a TODO.
Output: district persons (sch_grade, age_3_18) and county persons (sch_grade, age_18_24), written to _data/intermediate/.

title: Synthetic Population
text:
2. Classify students


Show code
# Same rules as PopulationSim's PersonType_Label (2_InputPreperation_Seed2.ipynb, person-type rules):
# SCHG 1-14 is pre-college and SCHG 15 or higher is college. K-12 is pre-college at ages 6-18;
# University student is college at age 16 or older.
# College: SCHG 15 (undergraduate) and 16 (beyond bachelor's), at any age. Age is counted separately.
persons["grade_15_plus"] = persons["sch_grade"].ge(15)
persons["age_18_24"] = persons["age"].between(18, 24)
# Nursery/preschool (SCHG 1) through grade 12 (SCHG 14), at any age. Matches DOE's totalk12 + preschool
# and NCES's K-12 + PK. Age is counted separately below, so this flag has no age condition.
persons["grade_1_14"] = persons["sch_grade"].between(1, 14)
persons["age_3_18"] = persons["age"].between(3, 18)

title: Geography
Geography
text:
Overview
This script builds the geographic crosswalk that every later step in this project joins against.

Objective: tie every Census block in the Wasatch Front region (Box Elder, Davis, Weber, Salt Lake, and Utah counties) to the school district and county it falls in, and to the K-12 school(s) and college(s) located in it — so that PopulationSim’s synthetic population (3_synthetic.qmd) and real enrollment data (2_enrollment.qmd) can both be rolled up to district/county level as exact joins, with no area-weighting or estimation involved.
What it pulls: county, school district, Travel Analysis Zone (TAZ), and Census block boundaries; K-12 school and college locations from both UGRC/SGID (the state-preferred source) and NCES (kept alongside, not as a replacement, so schools and colleges can also be joined back to federal CCD/IPEDS data by ID); and the WFRC/MAG travel demand model boundary, used later to handle Box Elder County’s partial coverage in that model. TAZ boundaries come from WFRC’s WasatchFrontTAZ feature service rather than the TDM-GEO-AnalysisZones repo directly, so the pull stays current without tracking that repo’s releases — TAZID is what is kept as a reference layer. The synthetic join uses MAZ, not TAZ.
Output: two crosswalks, one per use. _data/intermediate/crosswalk_school.csv maps each K-12 school (UGRC, NCES public, NCES private) and each MAZ to its district. _data/intermediate/crosswalk_college.csv maps each college (UGRC, NCES) and each MAZ to its county. MAZ rows appear in both files, so PopulationSim output rolls up through MAZ rather than through blocks. Section 10 checks coverage and maps the study area (Figure 1).

title: Geography
text:
3. Travel Analysis Zone (TAZ) boundaries


Show code
taz_boundary_path = paths["raw"] / "geometry" / "taz_boundary.gpkg"

# 1. Download only if not already cached locally
if not taz_boundary_path.exists():
    taz_url = (
        "https://services1.arcgis.com/taguadKoI1XFwivx/ArcGIS/rest/services/"
        "WasatchFrontTAZ/FeatureServer/0/query"
    )
    taz_pages = []
    offset = 0
    while True:
        page = gpd.read_file(
            f"{taz_url}?where=1=1&outFields=*&f=geojson"
            f"&orderByFields=FID&resultOffset={offset}&resultRecordCount=2000"
        )
        if page.empty:
            break
        taz_pages.append(page)
        offset += len(page)
        if len(page) < 2000:
            break
    all_taz = pd.concat(taz_pages, ignore_index=True).to_crs(constants["crs"])

    count_resp = requests.get(f"{taz_url}?where=1=1&returnCountOnly=true&f=json").json()
    assert len(all_taz) == count_resp["count"], (len(all_taz), count_resp["count"])

    all_taz["county_fips"] = all_taz["CO_FIPS"].astype(int).astype(str).str.zfill(3)

    all_taz.to_file(taz_boundary_path)

# 2. Read + filter in one step, pushed down to SQLite
county_list_sql = ", ".join(f"'{fips}'" for fips in county_fips)

        all_blocks.set_geometry(all_blocks.centroid),

title: Enrollment
Enrollment
text:
Overview
This script produces the “real enrollment” half of the validation schema — the numbers PopulationSim’s synthetic population (3_synthetic.qmd) gets compared against.

Objective: get district-level K-12 enrollment and county-level college enrollment from real, non-synthetic sources, joined through the school and college crosswalks built in 1_geography.qmd.
What it pulls: Utah DOE enrollment (public schools only, from UGRC’s own per-school counts), NCES enrollment by district (public via CCD, private via the Private School Universe Survey); USHE (student home ZIP code, not institution location — a different geography than everything else in this project) and NCES/IPEDS enrollment by county.
Known gaps: NCES private-school enrollment is school-location-based, not residence-based, and a handful of statewide online-only private programs still need manual review before being trusted at face value (see section 3); USHE data is Academic Year 2025, not 2023-24 — no 2023-24 USHE extract exists in what WFRC has on file, so this is a real year mismatch against the ~2023 vintage used everywhere else, not an oversight.
Output: one table of district-level enrollment, one table of county-level enrollment, both written to _outputs/.

# Public schools only
ugrc_public_schools = gpd.read_file(
    paths["raw"] / "geometry" / "ugrc_school.gpkg",
    sql="""
        SELECT * FROM ugrc_school
        WHERE privateschool = 'False'
          AND onlineschool IS NOT 'Y'
    """,
)

# Join school -> district via the school crosswalk (point-in-polygon, one row per school) rather than
# matching the school's own `leaname` text against the district boundary's `name` text.
doe_crosswalk = school_crosswalk[
    (school_crosswalk["Unit"] == "school") & (school_crosswalk["Source"] == "UGRC")
]
assert (doe_crosswalk.groupby("ID")["District Name"].nunique() <= 1).all(), (
    "UGRC school ID maps to two districts"
)
doe_crosswalk = doe_crosswalk.drop_duplicates(subset=["ID"])

# The UGRC layer repeats some school IDs. Exact copies (Minersville, 201, is listed twice with the same
# count) are dropped so they are not double-counted. Separate records that share an ID (Grouse Creek,
# 218, an elementary and a secondary with different counts) are both kept and summed.
ugrc_unique = (
    ugrc_public_schools[["schoolid", "schoolname", "totalk12", "preschool"]]
    .drop_duplicates()
    .assign(doe_students=lambda df: df["totalk12"] + df["preschool"].fillna(0))
)

# Left join, so schools with no crosswalk match are kept visible instead of silently dropped
doe_schools = (
    ugrc_unique.assign(schoolid=lambda df: df["schoolid"].astype("Int64").astype(str))
    .merge(doe_crosswalk[["ID", "District Name"]], how="left", left_on="schoolid", right_on="ID")
)
assert len(doe_schools) == len(ugrc_unique), "school join changed the row count"

unmatched_doe_schools = doe_schools[doe_schools["District Name"].isna()]
print(
    f"DOE schools with no district match: {len(unmatched_doe_schools)} "
    f"({unmatched_doe_schools['doe_students'].sum():,.0f} students, excluded from district totals)"
)

# groupby drops the unmatched rows (NaN district), so they are excluded from the totals below
doe_enrollment_by_district = (
    doe_schools.groupby("District Name")["doe_students"]
    .sum()
    .rename("doe_enrollment")
    .reset_index()

text:
2. K-12 — NCES enrollment by district


Show code
# Matches constants["data_year"] -- the vintage pulled in 1_geography.qmd
nces_public_school = gpd.read_file(paths["raw"] / "geometry" / "nces_public_school.gpkg")

nces_crosswalk = school_crosswalk[school_crosswalk["Source"] == "NCES public"]
assert (nces_crosswalk.groupby("ID")["District Name"].nunique() <= 1).all(), (
    "NCES public ID maps to two districts"
)
nces_crosswalk = nces_crosswalk.drop_duplicates(subset=["ID"])

# DOE totalk12 is K-12 only: it equals the sum of k and grades 1-12 on every public, non-online row, and
# it excludes preschool. NCES TOTAL includes PreK, plus other codes (UG, AE, G13), so NCES is summed
# over KG-G12 to match the DOE definition. NCES codes a grade the school doesn't offer as -2; those
# cells count as zero students.
nces_k12_grades = ["KG"] + [f"G{i:02d}" for i in range(1, 13)]
assert (nces_public_school[nces_k12_grades] >= -2).all().all(), "NCES K-12 grade has an unexpected code"
nces_public_school["K12"] = nces_public_school[nces_k12_grades].clip(lower=0).fillna(0).sum(axis=1)

# PK (preschool) uses the same -2 "not offered" rule as the grades, so negative codes count as zero
assert (nces_public_school["PK"] >= -2).all(), "NCES PK has an unexpected code"
nces_public_school["PK_students"] = nces_public_school["PK"].clip(lower=0).fillna(0)
nces_public_school["nces_students"] = nces_public_school["K12"] + nces_public_school["PK_students"]

nces_enrollment_by_district = (
    nces_public_school[["NCESSCH", "nces_students"]]
    .drop_duplicates()
    .assign(NCESSCH=lambda df: df["NCESSCH"].astype(str))
    .merge(
        nces_crosswalk[["ID", "District Name"]],
        left_on="NCESSCH",
        right_on="ID",
    )
    .groupby("District Name")["nces_students"]
    .sum()
    .rename("nces_enrollment")
    .reset_index()
)

This is the page the site is actually built around — where the real enrollment numbers (2_enrollment.qmd) and PopulationSim’s synthetic estimates (3_synthetic.qmd) get compared.

Objective: for each school district, compare real (Utah DOE / NCES) K-12 enrollment against PopulationSim’s synthetic K-12 student count (the real test, since that’s uncontrolled) and against its synthetic age 3-18 population (a sanity bound, since that’s controlled — not expected to match exactly). Same comparison for colleges by county, real (USHE / NCES-IPEDS) vs. synthetic sch_grade count (SCHG 15 and higher) and age 18-24 population.
What it reads: the real district and county tables from 2_enrollment.qmd and the synthetic district and county tables from 3_synthetic.qmd, all in _data/intermediate/.
Box Elder: reported separately from the other four counties, since its real and synthetic numbers are both scoped differently there (model region vs. full county) — a single pooled number would misrepresent it either way.
Output: this page itself — the published comparison tables and charts, not another intermediate file.
